newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile snow-hit Refugio gold mine still closed.
newsitem.headline: Chile snow-hit Refugio gold mine still closed.

text.p: Chile's Refugio gold mine, which shut down over a week ago after heavy snow, remained closed Monday as strong winds prevented workers from clearing the road to the pit, said a mine official.
The company hopes that buses from headquarters in Copiapo will be able to reach the mine in the next couple of days, said human resources manager Anibal Avendano.
"The mine is still closed. We hope to try and get the buses up there tomorrow or Wednesday," said Avendano by telephone from Copiapo.
Around 100 miners are stranded at the base camp at the mine which is built on an inhospitable plateau high in the Andes close to the border with Argentina.
Blizzards dumped several meters of snow on the open-cast pit and access roads, forcing the evacuation of the workers from the mine to the camp.
Refugio is owned equally by Canada's Bema Gold Corp and Amax Gold.
The mine processes 30,000 tonnes of mineral daily and is designed to produce 230,000 ounces of gold a year when running at full capacity.
